rationale: Provisional best-supported non-AI for the named Workload Service Assurance feature. HCL docs describe deadline calculations, job promotion and priority/resource assignment, conventional scheduling mechanics. Broader HWA 10 AI anomaly detection exists but is not attributed to this feature; do not transfer suite AI. Neither lane documented the whole product/included functionality, so retain weak/forced non-AI pending adjudication.
version_scope: Record supplies no product version; 'Milestone #8' is not treated as a version. Feature docs are HWA v10.2.6 and broader AI source is HWA 10.
issues: Product-level included-feature coverage incomplete; binary negative remains weak/forced.
Broader HWA AI anomaly-detection evidence does not establish AI in the identified optional Service Assurance feature; applicability unresolved.

sources.excerpt: The workload service assurance feature is enabled and disabled by the global option enWorkloadServiceAssurance. It is enabled by default. ... calculates a critical start time ... promoted job is assigned additional operating system resources and its submission is prioritized.
sources.applicability: Official feature-specific HWA v10.2.6 documentation describes deterministic deadline/priority operation; does not cover all product features.

sources.excerpt: HWA 10 introduces AI-powered anomaly detection for workloads ... AI Data Advisory ... big data machine learning analytics technologies applied to the data from Workload Automation.
sources.applicability: Official broader suite AI feature is potential conflicting evidence, but retained material does not connect it to the named Service Assurance feature.

sources.excerpt: Workload service assurance is an optional feature that allows you to identify critical jobs and to ensure that they are processed in a timely manner. (Milestone #8)
